first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly signaling friction in the entry funnel. Memory_31 and memory_86 both document durable activation and completion gains from simplification, making them the highest-confidence, most directly applicable interventions available. Verifying these two will confirm whether the original field-reduction and streamlining approaches remain valid, since competitive and seasonal conditions may have shifted. Simplify_onboarding is preferable to promotional_pricing (which risks margin and may not address the underlying activation decline) and to referral_incentive (which targets established customers, not the current intake problem). Enterprise_sales_assist addresses a different segment and doesn't solve the SMB activation headwind. Activation_messaging is lower-confidence than addressing the structural onboarding drop. A standard_experiment scope allows real signal without over-committing when completion metrics are declining.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both memories are reliable: exp_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB signup simplification; exp_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention on shortened onboarding. The 4% QoQ drop in onboarding completion is the most direct signal of friction, and simplification has the strongest empirical foundation across two independent experiments. Memory_86 in particular demonstrates retention gain, addressing the long-term value risk inherent in aggressive interventions. Activation_messaging (memory_91) can compound gains from onboarding improvement. Promotional_pricing risks margin and does not address the underlying completion decline. Enterprise_sales_assist is out of scope for the current SMB-driven activation headwind. A standard_experiment preserves learning velocity while the verified approach carries low downside risk based on durable prior results.
